fixed_launch_cost_usd.assumption: The sum of the thirteen NRE lines above at each end (low $4,360, base $9,930, high $22,300, rounded). Inventory for the first 300-1,000 sets (about $2,600-8,700 at landed cost) is working capital and lives in the landed cost, not here, so break-even units are not double-counted. The design filing and trademark ($1,150-6,900) could be phased into months 1-3 after launch under the US 12-month grace period, which would cut the pre-sale figure to about $3,250-15,400; they are budgeted up front because the filing date fixes the profile on paper, not because it stops a year-one clone (it does not, premortem[1]). The brief states no launch budget, so nothing here is checked against one.

price_usd.assumption: Inside the buyer's band: $19.99 is the most they pay with no visible reason and is the launch and coupon-day price for the first 60 days; $24.99 is the most they pay with the reason in the tile (buyer.price_psychology: a side profile of the arm over a thick edge with daylight under it, the thickness as a number). Base is now the top of the band, not $23.99, because critic K3 is right that the plan only works with the price at the top: at $24.99 the set is 1.43x the $17.49 anchor (scout.price_ladder, gate.price_vs_anchor, kahneman.anchoring) and needs the hero's no-fold 26 mm roll in the thumbnail to carry it; competition read $19.99-22.99 as 'mid-priced' against the $42-60 rails (F3, F26, ariely.relativity) and its 0.12 win probability was read at $19.99-21.99, so at $24.99 it is nearer 0.09, which the forecast's share already allows for. There is no high above $24.99 because the buyer's ceiling is $24.99 and the engine would reject it.

referral_rate.assumption: Scout's fetched 15% Office Products referral rate for 2026 (F17); the high is the $0.30 per-item minimum, which cannot bite inside the $15-25 band and is kept only for a clearance price.

fba_fee_usd.assumption: For the recommended 2-piece set, re-cubed after critic K8. The re-sectioned L is a 126 x 71 x 300 mm envelope per pad (100 mm top plus the 26 mm lip in front of the desk face; 26 mm top plus the 45 mm lip drop); two nest only as a Z (one upright, one inverted, lips at opposite ends, a 19 mm gap between the tops where the card sits) at 152 x 71 x 300 mm internal, so the supplier's 32 x 11 x 6.5-7.5 cm mailer (F25) cannot hold the pair. External about 15.7 x 7.6 x 30.6 cm (6.2 x 3.0 x 12.0 in) with E-flute walls = about 215-230 in3, a dimensional weight of 1.55-1.65 lb (divisor 139) against about 490 g (1.08 lb) actual, so the set is billed in the LARGE STANDARD 1.5-2 lb band, not the 1-1.25 lb band the first pass assumed and not the 1.25-1.5 lb band either unless the box is held at or under 208 in3. The 1-1.5 lb and 1.5-2 lb rows were not in scout's snippet (F18), so the fee is interpolated between the fetched $4.60 (12-16 oz) and $6.97 (3 lb) rows: 1.25-1.5 lb about $4.95, 1.5-2 lb about $5.50-5.60, 2-2.5 lb about $6.10-6.40, each plus the 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge from 17 April 2026 (F19). Base $5.75 = the 1.5-2 lb band with surcharge. Low $5.10 = the 1.25-1.5 lb row with surcharge, reachable only if the Z-nest is held at 148-152 x 69-71 mm internal with 2-3 mm of compression at the rolls and 1.5 mm E-flute (about 15.2 x 7.3 x 30.3 cm, 205 in3). High $6.90 = the 2-2.5 lb band if B-flute walls, a sleeve or Amazon's own cubing take the box past 278 in3, with the quarter widening the standard requires for a row not fetched. The single (v1_single) lands in the 1.25-1.5 lb band at about 190 in3. Scout's $3.68 small-standard low applies to no version: the L is 71 mm tall and even the flat 20 mm sample exceeds the small-standard thickness limit. STALE until the exact 2026 rows are read on the Seller Central rate card.

storage_alloc_usd.assumption: Stale: scout did not fetch storage this run and carried over about $0.78 per cu ft Jan-Sep and $2.40 Oct-Dec, widened by a quarter as the standard requires. The Z-nest set box is about 3.65 litres = 0.129 cu ft (up from 0.095 on the first box); a blended $1.20 per cu ft over an average three-month dwell for a 1,000-set order selling over six months gives about $0.46 a set; low is a 300-set order sold through in eight weeks at the Jan-Sep rate; high is Q4 storage at $2.40 for three months plus the 181-day aged-inventory surcharge if velocity lands at the forecast's low end.

return_rate.assumption: Desk accessories without electronics run about 3-6% returns (rule of thumb, no source); this product's specific return reason is fear 2 and N2, 'does the lip fit my edge' (post.return_reason), pushed down by the honest 18-38 mm fit limit on the tile, the card and the first bullet (cialdini.reciprocity) and up to 11% if the lip rides up on real desks with aprons or bullnose edges; the engine models the cost as rate x (0.4 x price + 0.6 x landed). Warranty claims are NOT returns and are carried in landed as the reserve line.

ad_rate.assumption: Year-one advertising as a share of all revenue, volume-weighted across the ramp: months 1-3 at 45-60% ACoS on nearly every order because a zero-review tile buys each click (gate.social_proof, rogers.innovators), months 4-6 near 30%, months 7-12 at 15-20% once organic rank on 'elbow pad for desk' carries about half the orders, which blends to about 25% (the knowledge base's 40-80% launch and 15-30% steady-state bands for a commodity); low assumes Vine and the card's review trigger get us past 100 reviews by month 6 and organic takes over early; high is the clone-wave price war in which every order is bought against $12.99-14.99 twins (competition.price_war). The founder's 30-40% margin target is measured before this line, and the engine's 15% floor is measured after it, which is why the floor is a year-two number at 15-20% ads, not a year-one one at 25%.

term_monthly_units.assumption: No tracker page was readable, so est_monthly_units is blank for every competitor (scout.gaps); this is a Fermi estimate from review velocity (forecast.fermi, forecast.reference_class): JIKIOU 791 ratings in about 15 months is about 53 a month (F7); VAYDEER's 2,045 is carried unchanged from 23 September (F11) so no velocity exists in the file, and 2,045 over a 2020 ASIN averages under 30 a month, so it is taken at 25-40 a month (critic K16), not the 40-80 of the first pass; EdgeRest 226 in about 24 months (F2); ArmCloud unknown (F6); nine look-alike 2-packs (F9) and the gel and flat pads from the earlier run (F12-F14) at an assumed 1,800 units a month with no count behind it. At an assumed 2-5% review-per-order rate (base 3.5%) that is roughly JIKIOU 1,500, VAYDEER 900, EdgeRest 250, ArmCloud 150, the look-alikes 1,800 and the rest 600 units a month, about 5,200 on 'elbow pad for desk'; the band is -45% / +65% because a 2% review rate doubles every line and about half the base rests on no count at all. A unit is a listing's unit, so a 2-pack counts once. One human read of VAYDEER's and JIKIOU's counts today and in four weeks replaces the biggest guess.

share_m6.assumption: A new entrant reaches 1-5% in months 1-3 and 3-10% by months 6-12 only if click-through and conversion beat the median; today the buyer's 0.65 click goes to VAYDEER or JIKIOU (buyer.purchase_probability_current, gate.social_proof), competition gives us 0.12 as the chosen tile before clones (nearer 0.09 at $24.99), and with about 50-80 reviews by month 6 (Vine plus a 5% review rate on the ramp) we are still inside the chasm (moore.chasm), so base 2.5% is below the knowledge base's midpoint; high assumes the hero's no-fold tile (innovaty thumbnail_visibility high) and the daylight-under-the-arm image (buyer.memory_hook) put us on page one by month 4. These are PRE-clone-window numbers; the engine applies competition's 35% haircut on top.

share_m12.assumption: 3-10% by month 12 if CTR and conversion beat the median; base 4% assumes about 100-150 reviews by month 12 against JIKIOU's 791 and VAYDEER's 2,045 (past the 30-review floor, still far from the leader), a 4.5+ rating because C1 and C3 are answered in the build and C2 by the uncoated knit, and page-one placement on the term at $24.99; low is page two at 15-30 reviews with ads doing all the work; high is the row's own JIKIOU trajectory (791 reviews in 15 months, F7). Pre-clone numbers: after the 35% haircut the base is about 2.6%, which is the number to plan cash around.

monthly_units_m6.assumption: Term volume times share at each end: 2,800 x 1%, 5,200 x 2.5%, 8,500 x 5%; sets a month in month 6, before the clone haircut the engine applies.

monthly_units_m12.assumption: Term volume times share at each end: 2,800 x 1.5%, 5,200 x 4%, 8,500 x 8%; sets a month in month 12, before the clone haircut.

annual_units_y1.assumption: The engine's linear ramp from zero to the month-6 figure and on to the month-12 figure, summed (6 x month-6 plus 3.5 x month-12): months 1-3 are innovator-only volume (rogers.innovators); after competition's 35% haircut the base year is about 1,000 sets.

forecast.seasonality_note: Scout did not confirm seasonality for the term (search_terms notes); the earlier run assumed a mild January 'organise my life' and September office-setup uptick (knowledge base seasonality), and Q4 raises storage cost rather than demand for a desk pad (forecast.reference_class: no gifting signal in any listing scout read), so no seasonal adjustment is applied beyond the ranges.
forecast.reasoning: Outside in (forecast.reference_class, forecast.fermi): scout has no tracker volumes, so term volume is a Fermi estimate from review velocity, about 5,200 units a month on 'elbow pad for desk' (2,800-8,500) at an assumed 2-5% review-per-order rate with VAYDEER taken at 25-40 reviews a month, and that rate plus the uncounted look-alike half are the assumptions to audit first. Our share: the buyer clicks VAYDEER or JIKIOU 65% of the time today (gate.social_proof) and competition gives us 0.12 as the chosen tile at launch, falling to 0.07 once twins arrive; a zero-review tile at $24.99 starts on page two, months 1-3 are innovator-only (rogers.innovators, moore.chasm), Vine plus the card's review trigger bring 50-80 reviews by month 6 and 100-150 by month 12, which keeps us inside the chasm against 791 and 2,045 but past the 30-review floor, so 2.5% of the term by month 6 (30-425 sets, base 130) and 4% by month 12 (40-680, base 210), year one 320-4,900, base 1,500 sets. These share numbers are the PRE-clone window: competition rates copycat risk high, twins in 1-6 months at $12.99-16.99 and a 35% haircut, and the engine applies that haircut itself (monte_carlo_cloned), so the cloned base is about 135 sets in month 12 and 1,000 in the year; the wave is deliberately not baked into the shares to avoid a double haircut. Set versus single: the pair is the row's form (nine of twelve tiles, F9) and the two boxes cost almost the same to fulfil (the Z-nested set at about $5.75 in the 1.5-2 lb band against about $5.35 for one L in the 1.25-1.5 lb band, both large standard because the L is 71 mm tall), so the pair spreads that fee over two pads; the single at $17.99 would sell one pad an order, fight the 2,045-review leader at its own price (competition threat high) and the buyer has a two-forearm problem (N6), so the pair is recommended. Lean versus full spec: the recommended v1_lean (I1, I3, I5, I6) lands at about $8.70 a set at base against $11.00 for innovaty's full v1_now, and only the lean build can reach the engine's 30% landed rail ($7.50 at $24.99) at MOQ 1,000 on the 26% tariff scenario; the engine will show that neither clears the 15% post-advertising floor at year-one ad rates, which is why the fix is the tariff scenario, the MOQ-1,000 EXW, the price at the top of the band and a year-two ad rate together, not the pack count or the spec.

phases.phase: DFM and quotes: profile CAD for the re-sectioned L (26 mm corner, 3.5-degree wedge), two factory quotes on the lean spec and the full spec at MOQ 300 and 1,000, written confirmation that $5.75 is per set (F25), a licensed broker's written classification on 9404.90.20 versus 8473.30.51 with the Section 301 list footnote and the July-2026 12.5% layer (F27-F33)

weeks.assumption: 2-4 calendar weeks before the multiplier (base 3), times 1.35 (forecast.planning_fallacy); the broker opinion and the second quote run in parallel with the CAD; high is a broker who wants a binding-ruling request drafted before committing.

phases.phase: Prototypes and fit tests: the new profile template, two sample rounds air-freighted, seating on a 25 mm square edge and a 38 mm R5 eased edge, the edge-load bottoming test on the single core (I1), and weighing and cubing the Z-nest box against the live FBA rate card

weeks.assumption: 3-6 weeks before the multiplier (base 4), times 1.35 (forecast.planning_fallacy); a foam template turns in days, the air freight and the second round set the floor; high (+50%) is a third round because the first L seats crooked on the eased edge or the box cubes over the line.

phases.phase: Lab gates: compression set, 80,000-cycle fatigue, COF on five surfaces, 20 washes and pilling, 14-day sebum ageing, chamber sniff (I1, I3, I6); if the bottoming test failed, I2 is pulled in and the 500 h humidity-aged peel (three weeks on its own) joins the critical path; photography, listing copy, the design filing and Brand Registry run in parallel

weeks.assumption: 3-9 weeks before the multiplier (base 4), times 1.35 (forecast.planning_fallacy): low is every gate passing with the 14-day sebum ageing as the critical path; high (+125%) is one failed gate, which costs a re-sample, air freight and a re-test (5-6 weeks), and if that gate pulled I2 forward, the 500 h peel on the cradle-bonded shell on top. The first pass fitted this high to the 39-week rail (critic K12); this one does not.

phases.phase: Production: template sign-off, first run of 300-1,000 sets with the 7-day open-rack foam rest (I6), pre-shipment inspection, packing in the Z-nest mailer with the card and no bag, 30 per 63 x 48 x 40 cm carton

weeks.assumption: 4-7 weeks before the multiplier (base 5), times 1.35 (forecast.planning_fallacy); includes the seven rest days and a factory queue behind larger orders; high (+40%) is a failed pre-shipment inspection on the base-panel seam and a partial re-sew.

phases.phase: Sea freight LCL China to US West Coast, customs entry under the broker's classification, FBA check-in and the first organic order

weeks.assumption: 5-8 weeks before the multiplier (base 6), times 1.35 (forecast.planning_fallacy); port-to-port 30-45 days on scout's stale freight assumption plus one to two weeks of receiving; high (+33%) is a customs exam on a new importer with a contested HTS line or FBA receiving in the Q4 queue.

weeks_to_first_sale.assumption: The five phases summed: 17-34 weeks before the multiplier (base 22, inside the knowledge base's 20-34 because the tooling is a foam template, not a steel injection tool), times the 1.35 planning-fallacy multiplier stated above (forecast.planning_fallacy): 23 / 30 / 46. The high of 46 BREAKS the engine's 39-week first-sale rail: it is one failed lab gate (a re-sample round plus, if I2 is pulled in, the 500 h peel) on top of a third prototype round and a Q4 receiving queue, each of which the file names elsewhere, so the number is estimated, not fitted (critic K12). At base, 30 weeks clears the rail by nine.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the single 60 kg/m3 core took a permanent dent at the R20 roll on pads that spent a summer in a 30 C room, the arm found the desk corner again by 4 pm, and three matching one-stars on 'flattened where it goes over the edge' sank the rating to 4.1: C1, the cluster the hero exists to fix, delivered by the layer we cut to save $0.55 a set (I1, I2, N5).
premortem.mitigation: The edge-load bottoming test on the T1 lean sample (25 mm bar, 30 N, 60 min at 35 C, residual >= 8 mm over the corner on the 25 mm square and 38 mm R5 edges), ISO 1856 compression set <= 5% and ISO 3385 80,000 cycles on the roll zone, all before the template is signed off; if any fails, I2 (the HR 45 core under the 10 mm shell, cradle-bonded with the sprayed water-based PU adhesive) is pulled into v1 at about +$0.55 a set with its humidity-aged peel gate (>= 1 N/cm after 500 h at 40 C / 80% RH, ASTM D903) and the plan is re-costed as v1_now less the zip; the memory layer cut as its own L either way so no bond is ever in peel at the roll (innovaty durability_review).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: The foam lab line plus the v1.1 gates in reserve if I2 comes forward, plus the cradle; a retained-sample programme on two lots.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and three 2-packs with a rounded no-fold corner appeared on page one between months 2 and 5 at $12.99-14.99, re-cut from an open foam die, took the price-sensitive two-thirds of our clicks, and we sold 35% fewer sets than planned. This agrees with competition's read: copycat risk high, first clone in 1-6 months, clone price $12.99-16.99, haircut 35% (competition.copycat_risk, price_war).
premortem.mitigation: Year-one defence is only what works inside a 1-6 month window, because a pending design application is not enforceable (critic K9, competition: 'protects year two, not launch'): (1) the review lead, a 50-reviews-a-month velocity target against JIKIOU's 53 from Vine, the card's trigger and the request button (moore.chasm, cialdini.social_proof); (2) the proof images a $3 clone cannot shoot honestly, image 2's ruler on a 26 mm corner section and image 3's sectioned pad and bare base on glass, so a thin single-density twin reads as the pad the buyer was burned by (gate.image_2_to_6, law.shape_memory); (3) Brand Registry for listing hijacks and counterfeit of the brand name only, not for design copies; (4) price discipline, no match below $19.99, because the margin cannot fund a war (ariely.relativity); (5) the Alibaba 'elbow pad desk' page watched weekly as the 6-10 week leading indicator (competition.watch_signals). The design application is filed before launch so the profile is fixed on paper, and it becomes a takedown tool only when it issues, about 16-20 months out: a year-two tool, costed in tooling_and_nre[7].

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: The year-one items are inside the photography and Vine lines plus an hour a week of watch time; the design filing and trademark ($1,150-6,900 with expedited examination in the high) are the year-two part; the haircut itself is simulated by the engine, not mitigated here.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the Z-nested box for two 26 mm Ls cubed at 2.1 lb dimensional weight instead of 1.6 because the factory used B-flute and a sleeve, Amazon re-tiered the set, and the fulfilment fee came in $0.35-1.15 a set above plan on every unit: the packaging-over-the-line obituary, on a box that is already one band above the one the first pass assumed (critic K8).
premortem.mitigation: Hold the Z-nest at 148-152 x 69-71 x 300 mm internal in 1.5 mm E-flute with the card in the gap between the tops and nothing else in the box; weigh and cube the T1 box against the live rate card before the template is signed off (timeline phase 2); target 208 in3 or under so the set drops to the 1.25-1.5 lb row, which is worth about $0.65 a set; cap pad weight at 200 g with the 60 kg/m3 build rather than the sample's 250 g (irrelevant to the band while dimensional weight governs, but it keeps the actual weight under it); never let a sleeve or a second card add a layer.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: One dieline iteration and a cubing check; the fee difference is already inside the fba_fee_usd range.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the broker put the pad on 8473.30.51 (List 3) instead of 9404.90.20, or a new layer landed between the deposit and the entry, and the China stack on our line went from the 26% we planned to 37.5-44.5%, adding $0.60-1.00 a set at the lean EXW, and the first 1,000 sets landed at a loss before advertising: the origin-tariff obituary, on a stack that has changed three times in 2026 alone (F27, F28, F29).
premortem.mitigation: A licensed broker's written classification on 9404.90.20 (scenario B, 6% + List 4A 7.5% + the 12.5% July-2026 tier = 26%) with the 9903.88.xx footnote read from the HTS page, or a CBP binding-ruling request if the broker will not commit, before any deposit (F31, F33); scenario A (8473.30.51 free + List 3 25% + 12.5% = 37.5%) and scenario C on List 3 (6307.90.98 at 7% + 25% + 12.5% = 44.5%, not searched this run) are the cases the written opinion must rule out; the first order capped at 1,000 sets; a Vietnam or Indonesia foam-and-sewing second source sampled at the prototype stage so the second order can change origin; the price held at $24.99 rather than $19.99 so there is room to absorb one step; and the July-2026 12.5% layer tracked, since the CIT struck the Section 122 bridge in May 2026 and a refund scenario (13.5%) is live (F28).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Broker opinion $150-400 (a binding-ruling request is the founder's time plus the broker's hour) plus one Vietnam sample round and its air freight $200-1,400.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and a packaging or certification bullet was flagged under Amazon's environmental-claims policy and the listing sat suppressed for nine days in month 3 while the clones ranked: the suppressed-claim obituary (innovaty sustainability claims, critic K11).
premortem.mitigation: Word the box line as 'ships in a paper box with no plastic bag' and the cover line as 'cover made from fabric certified to OEKO-TEX Standard 100 (certificate on file)' in a bullet only, with the mill's certificate (number, scope, validity) in Seller Central and nothing on the tag, since the certificate is the mill's for the knit and not ours for the finished cover; never 'eco', 'green', 'plastic-free product' or 'certified cover'; keep 'replaceable cover' as the longevity claim once I4 ships and 'washable fabric' until then (innovation playbook 7).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: A copy review; nothing physical changes.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and we reached 38 reviews by month 6 and 90 by month 12 against VAYDEER's 2,045 and JIKIOU's 791, the tile never left page two on 'elbow pad for desk', ads bought every order at 45% and the forecast's month-12 volume never arrived: the review-velocity obituary (moore.chasm, gate.social_proof, competition watch_signals). It is also the obituary of the 15% floor, which only exists at a 15-20% ad rate that needs those reviews.
premortem.mitigation: Vine on 30 sets at launch; the card's review trigger with a QR beside the spec and the Limited Warranty (post.review_trigger, I5); Amazon's review-request button on every order; a $19.99 launch price for the first 60 days against the $24.99 list; and a hard check at month 4: under 30 reviews means the ad budget stops and the price war is not fought, so the loss is bounded.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Vine fee plus 30 sets at landed cost (in the NRE) plus a $5 launch discount on the first 300 sets.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the quoted supplier priced the lean spec at $6.20 a set, the broker put us on the 37.5% line, the Z-nest box billed at 1.5-2 lb, the set landed at $10 against a $24.99 price, and every unit lost money after the 15% referral, the $5.75 fulfilment fee and the launch advertising: the plan was signed on a $5.75 quote for a different, simpler pad (F25) and the 30-40% margin was never there.
premortem.mitigation: No deposit until two numbers are in writing, and both are NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT (critic K3): (a) a licensed broker's classification on 9404.90.20 with the stack at or under 26%, and (b) a lean-spec EXW at or under $4.50 a set at MOQ 1,000 from one of two factories (I expect $4.00-4.80, so this is set where the number lands, not where it is hoped to land). Together they put v1_lean at about $7.25-7.40 landed, under the engine's 30% rail at $24.99, and no more than that. For the 15% post-advertising floor to clear, the engine's arithmetic also needs: the price at $24.99 with the thickness proof in the tile (not $23.99, not $19.99 beyond the 60-day launch), the ad rate at 15-20% (a year-two number that arrives only past about 100 reviews at 50 a month), returns at or under 6%, and the box at or under 208 in3 so the fee drops to the 1.25-1.5 lb row; year one at 25% ads is a planned loss at every combination of the two gates. What the plan does at each end: at $4.00 and 26% it ships v1_lean at $24.99 and funds I2 from the first margin; at $4.80 or at 37.5% it ships only if the July layer is vacated (13.5%) or the box makes the lower row, else it does not ship from China at this price; above $5.00 at MOQ 1,000 on the lean spec, or if the bottoming test forces I2 and the EXW rises past $5.00, the founder re-briefs on origin (Vietnam second source) or price (the $42-60 rail category, which is a different product and a different buyer).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: A second factory's sample rounds and air freight; the broker opinion is in the tariff item above.

premortem.obituary: v1.1 only (I4 is not in the recommended version): it is twelve months after the zipped cover ships and the coil zip on the lip jammed on the knit edge or its tape stitching let go on the first wash for about one buyer in twenty, and the washable-cover delighter became the one-star pattern (I4, N3, gate.reviews_negative_first).
premortem.mitigation: Before I4 ships in v1.1: a named SBS or YKK #3 coil on the 370 mm U, the slider garage and bar-tacked ends innovaty specified, 500 open-close cycles, 20 washes and the 50-refit test by an untrained user on the sample, the cord puller instead of metal, and the care step shown on the card (cold wash, air dry); if the refit fails, the replacement sleeve stays the service part and the cover stays sewn closed.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: Branded zips add about $0.03-0.08 a pad on the v1.1 order plus the cycle and refit tests in the reserve lab line.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the $5.75 turned out to be per piece in the set configuration, not per set, the ambiguity scout flagged in F25; the real set EXW was $11.50 and nothing in the $15-25 band could carry it.
premortem.mitigation: A written pro-forma invoice stating EXW per 2-piece set, incoterm, MOQ, box and carton spec before any deposit, cross-checked against the two Alibaba 1-piece prices (F23, F24) which cap a bare pad at about $3.20.

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: An email and a pro-forma; an hour of the founder's time.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and 'does not fit my desk' was the top return reason: aprons, keyboard trays, bullnose edges and tops over 38 mm sent 9% of sets back and the stars fell with them (fear 2, N2, C3, post.return_reason).
premortem.mitigation: The honest fit limit (18-38 mm, square or eased up to R5, 50 mm of clear desk face, not bullnose) in the first bullet, on the card and as a dimensioned drawing in image 2 (innovaty honest_limitations, cialdini.reciprocity), a 'measure your edge' line in the back half of the title, and the R6 relief that seats eased edges flat (I1).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: The dimensioned drawing and the card artwork, inside the listing-graphics NRE line.

premortem.obituary: It is twelve months on and the two-year promise drew claims at 8% of sets because 'flattens' was never defined, every subjective claim was honoured with a pad and $7 of postage, the $0.40-a-set reserve was gone by month 8, and the wording was woven into a tag that could not be changed without a re-order: the written-warranty obituary (I5, critic K10).
premortem.mitigation: Designate it 'Limited Warranty' and state the terms on the card and pre-sale in the listing, as the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act requires for a written warranty on a consumer product over $15 (16 CFR 701-702): covered = more than 20% thickness loss at the roll measured against the card's printed ruler, or base-panel separation, within two years of delivery, photo required; remedy = one replacement pad (not a set) shipped from a small US stock; the sewn-in tag carries the spec line only so the wording can change without a re-order; claim rate re-read at month 6 and the reserve re-set from it; the cost is carried per unit in the warranty-reserve BOM line where the engine sees it (law.loss_aversion framing kept: the promise still answers N5).

mitigation_cost_usd.assumption: The warranty-wording review (in the compliance line), the ruler artwork on the card, and a 2-3% spare-pad stock held in the US from the first order; the per-claim cost itself is the reserve in landed, not here.

idea_rulings.deciding_number: +$0.55 a set at base (HR core $0.20 + shell $0.29 + sprayed bond $0.16, less the $0.48 single core, per pad, with overhead), a $30-200 cradle and a $150-400 humidity-aged peel gate, against a lean EXW gate of $4.50 at MOQ 1,000

regulatory: Prop 65 (California): polyurethane foam can carry listed flame retardants such as TDCPP; require the supplier's written declaration of no listed FR on the foam lot or carry the warning on the box; no CPSC or children's-product testing applies to an adult desk accessory with no magnets in v1 (regulatory baseline for a passive accessory, knowledge base timeline note).

FTC Textile Fiber Products Identification Act and country of origin: '100% polyester cover' and 'Made in China' on the woven tag and the box; the mill's OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certificate (number, scope, validity) kept on file in Seller Central for the bullet 'cover made from fabric certified to OEKO-TEX Standard 100', nothing on the tag and never 'certified cover'; no 'eco' or 'biodegradable' wording on PU foam (innovaty rejected_claims, critic K11).

Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act: the two-year 'if the foam flattens or the base peels we replace it' promise is a written warranty on a consumer product over $15, so it is designated 'Limited Warranty', its terms (what is covered: more than 20% thickness loss at the roll against the card's printed ruler, or base-panel separation, within two years of delivery, photo required; remedy: one replacement pad shipped from US stock; how to claim) are printed on the card and made available pre-sale in the listing (16 CFR 701-702), and the sewn-in tag carries the spec line only so the wording can change without a re-order; it is also honoured as written under Amazon's claims policy (critic K10). No FCC, UL or CE applies to a passive foam pad; if I7 ships in v2 the listing states the magnets are sewn captive and the product is not for children.
three_sentences_to_founder: Your 30-40% is a pre-advertising margin, and the money has moved against you since the last pass: the re-sectioned L (26 mm legs, 126 x 71 x 300 mm per pad) nests two-up only in a 15.7 x 7.6 x 30.6 cm box that cubes at about 1.6 lb dimensional weight, so the set is billed in the 1.5-2 lb large-standard band (about $5.75 a set, interpolated from the fetched rows and marked stale) instead of the 1-1.25 lb band assumed before; the fetched China stack is 26% on the likely line (9404.90.20: 6% + List 4A 7.5% + the 12.5% July-2026 tier), 37.5% if a broker puts it on 8473.30.51 (free + List 3 25% + 12.5%) and 13.5% only if the July layer is vacated; and innovaty's full spec is $7.00 a set EXW bottom-up at MOQ 300, so v1_now lands at about $11.00 a set ($7.20-17.40) against a $24.99 ceiling and never reaches the engine's 30% landed rail ($7.50) at any EXW I expect, even at MOQ 1,000.

So the version to cost and ship is v1_lean, not v1_now: the no-fold 26 mm-corner L, the vulcanised base on both faces, the spec tag with a properly worded Limited Warranty, and the no-smell build, with one 60 kg/m3 core and a sewn-closed wipe-clean knit; it lands at about $8.70 a set ($5.40-14.40) and about $7.25-7.40 at MOQ 1,000 on the 26% stack, the two-layer core (I2, about $0.55 a set) and the U-zip washable cover (I4, about $1.35 a set) become v1.1 funded from margin, I2 comes straight back if the single core fails the 30 N / 60 min bottoming test on the T1 sample, and because this version is no longer innovaty's v1_now, the orchestrator must reconcile innovaty's image 3 (two-band section) and image 4 (unzip step) before anything is shot.

Sign nothing until two numbers are in writing, a broker's classification on 9404.90.20 at or under 26% and a lean-spec EXW at or under $4.50 a set at MOQ 1,000 (I expect $4.00-4.80, so this is a coin toss, not a formality), and understand that both are necessary and neither is sufficient: the engine's 15% post-advertising floor also needs the price at $24.99 with the thickness proof in the tile, ads down to 15-20% (a year-two number that arrives only past about 100 reviews at 50 a month against JIKIOU's 53), returns at or under 6% and the box held under 208 in3 for the 1.25-1.5 lb row, so year one at 25% ads is a planned loss at every combination, the first sale lands at 23-46 weeks with the 1.35 multiplier applied and the 46 breaks the 39-week rail if one lab gate fails, and the plan is unrealistic as costed and FIX-FIRST, not dead.
